role_title: Non-fire seasonal field technician (forestry, recreation, trails, wildlife)
description: No non-fire seasonal hiring at USFS in 2025; 2,000 seasonals committed for 2026, all titled forestry technician, with short application windows. The classic first rung into field craft was closed for a season and reopened narrower

Trail miles maintained fell 22% in 2025, with named tacit skills lost (equipment operation, rock masonry) and no seasonal trail crews. Corps hours on the PCT fell from ~19,000 to ~4,000. Skills reproduced only by crew apprenticeship are lost in one or two seasons

role_title: Conservation corps member -> agency technician pathway
description: $400M AmeriCorps cuts and terminations in 2025; FY2026 status litigated with a stay to 2027-02-01. No published alumni outcome data found. Whether noncompetitive hiring eligibility for corps service remains usable is unverified

Federal under-30 share fell to 7.9% (Jan 2026) from 8.9% (Sep 2024), against 19.4% of the US labour force. Student-trainee occupations declined (as recorded by FH). Accessions were 122,598 vs ~250,000 typical. Federal entry for new graduates is severely narrowed

NPS lost more than a quarter of its employees; park rangers down 34.1% (PPS figures as recorded by FH). v1 rates visitor-services entry work as High CLD (kiosks, chatbots), so entry is squeezed from both sides

role_title: Collateral-duty red-card holder (non-fire staff with fire quals)
description: ~1,400-1,600 fire-qualified non-fire staff departed. USFS relies on ~10,000 non-fire staff with fire quals and asked resigned workers to return. Surge fire capacity built through collateral duty is eroding as non-fire field staff shrink

DOI consolidated bureau fire programmes into the US Wildland Fire Service (Jan 2026). USWFS/USFS qualification standards align from Jan 2027. Intra-federal fire mobility should become easier; mobility to state, Tribal and contract fire depends on NWCG portability, which already exists

v1 rates four Domain 6 entry tasks as Substitution at the primary-learning position (regulatory research synthesis; compliance drafting; policy research; comment triage). Statecraft-primary competencies carry CLD flags at 37% vs 20-22% for FC/DC. No environment-specific external corroboration yet (LM's lane)

role_title: Entry-level project, budget and grants assistant
description: The most portable foundation competencies in v1 (3.1.1 project planning; 3.1.2 budget; Supporting in 10 families, Core in none) carry CLD flags; 3.1.2 is High severity. The skills that move people between actors are learned in entry tasks AI is compressing

role_title: Federal NEPA coordinator / biologist / planner moving to state or local government
description: Probationary firings hit NEPA coordinators and biologists. States ran programmes to recruit displaced federal staff, and a partnership formed to place them in state and local government. USFS turned to state and community partners for work. Federal-specific statecraft must be re-enacted under state law (SC enactment question)

role_title: County / state-park recreation-site manager taking over federal sites
description: Pitkin County will manage the Maroon Bells Scenic Area from 2027 under a USFS special use permit. Sweetwater Lake went to Colorado Parks and Wildlife in 2024. Federal functions are devolving to counties and states, creating roles that need federal-site knowledge plus local statecraft

role_title: Senior federal policy, legal and science staff in Schedule Policy/Career
description: ~8,000 positions (97% GS-15+) moved into Schedule Policy/Career, including EPA legal staff (as recorded by FH). Changed tenure and accountability may push experienced statecraft holders to states, NGOs or private employers. The mobility effect is not yet evidenced

Colorado and Maryland froze state hiring in summer 2025 even as states courted displaced federal staff. Displaced federal applicants (many with degrees) compete for the same entry and mid-level openings, and degree filters may return
v1 rates collecting ESG/GHG data for sustainability reporting (3.6.2 T1) as High CLD: AI accounting tools compress a new field's primary literacy-building task

At least 26 states have dropped or reduced degree requirements. In Pennsylvania ~60% of new hires lack a degree after 92% of positions were de-degreed. In Colorado the share of hires without a degree was flat at 25% (2023-24). Competency-based minimum qualifications are spreading, but conversion to hires depends on assessments and manager practice

Under the Chance to Compete Act, self-assessment questionnaires are phased out. USA Hire expands from 138 to 412 series, and 34.3% of delegated-examining announcements used technical assessments in FY26 Q2 (as recorded by FH). Assessed skills, not self-ratings, become the federal gate: the point where a portable competency language can matter
